title: NeoMundi Evidence timestamp descriptor, version 1
description: Describes a detached OpenTimestamps proof and what it is bound to. The descriptor is a CONVENIENCE, not the evidence: the binding is established by the `.ots` proof itself, which commits to a digest readable at a fixed offset with no dependency. A descriptor that disagreed with the proof would be refused, never believed. Decrit une preuve OpenTimestamps detachee et ce a quoi elle est liee. Le descripteur est une COMMODITE, pas la preuve : la liaison est etablie par le fichier `.ots` lui-meme.

subject_name.description: File name of the timestamped subject. Informative: a rename does not break anything, since the digest is what binds.

subject_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the subject. The verifier recomputes it and compares it with the digest the proof commits to; a mismatch is a FAIL.

subject_kind.description: `evidence_attestation` timestamps the signed attestation, which is the preferred target: it binds the time claim to the signature rather than to the bytes alone.

proof_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the `.ots` file as written. Changes on every `upgrade`, which produces a NEW proof rather than overwriting the old one.

stamped_at_declared.description: When WE submitted the digest to the calendars. DECLARED BY US, and emphatically NOT the timestamp: the time a proof attests, once confirmed, comes from the Bitcoin chain and from nothing we write here. The `_declared` suffix is part of the field name so no reader can mistake it.

calendars_submitted.description: Calendars that accepted the digest. Only the 32-byte digest was transmitted -- never the archive, the manifest, or any pilot data.

calendars_silent.description: Calendars that did not answer. Recorded rather than hidden: a proof resting on one calendar is weaker than one resting on four.

state_at_stamping.description: `pending` at stamping time, always. A PENDING attestation means a calendar committed to including the digest in a future Bitcoin transaction -- IT ATTESTS NO DATE. Only a `bitcoin` attestation, obtained later by `upgrade`, carries a time claim; and verifying even that needs a block header, which this repository does not have.

upgraded_from.description: SHA-256 of the previous proof, when this one came from an `upgrade`. The earlier proof is never destroyed: it is a piece of evidence in its own right.

limits.description: What this timestamp does not establish. Must state at minimum that no eIDAS qualified timestamp is claimed: OpenTimestamps is not a qualified trust service provider under the regulation.
